title: Historic Deal Positions FIA World Endurance Championship for Record Decade of Growth as the Sport Enters its Golden Age
summary: Sport news The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, and the Automobile Club de l’Ouest (ACO), the founder and organiser of the 24 Hours of Le Mans, have today announced a major deal for the FIA World Endurance Championship (FIA WEC), securing another decade of growth.   The landmark agreement, which comes during a period of unprecedented growth for the championship, will ensure a common ambition to expand the partnership and drive its commercial success. It will run from the end of 2027, when the current agreement expires, to the end of 2037.    Under the extended partnership agreement, all regulatory processes will be overseen by FIA Working Groups, the FIA Endurance Commission, and will require the final approval of the FIA World Motor Sport Council. The homologation process has also been streamlined, with the FIA and ACO overseeing the homologation of all cars competing in the Hypercar class.   The renewed partnership will also deliver significantly increased branding for the FIA. This includes enhanced branding prominently displayed across key areas including parc fermé, the podium and the Safety Cars, as well as across broadcast coverage.   With an expanding fanbase, a wider pool of competitors, and a global calendar of iconic events, the championship is stronger than ever. Since its inception in 2012, it has set the global standard for long-distance circuit racing. Following the introduction of the Hypercar regulations in 2021, interest in the championship from motor sport fans and from the automotive world has surged.    FIA WEC’s trackside audience has grown 8% so far in 2026, with millions of fans following the championship globally. The fanbase for the championship is also evolving. This year, 44% of attendees are aged 34 or younger, while 40% are attending an FIA WEC event for the first time. The championship has secured the long-term loyalty of its existing fanbase, while building the next generation of endurance racing fans.   Eight of the world’s leading auto-manufacturers currently compete in Hypercar, the top category of FIA WEC. Following the addition of the LMGT3 class in 2024, the championship now counts no fewer than 14 marques in total on the starting grid. Two more giants of the automotive industry – Ford and McLaren – are set to join the Hypercar ranks in 2027.   For over 100 years, endurance racing has served as a proven testbed for technologies that transfer from track to road. This renewed agreement creates a solid framework for advancing hydrogen powertrains in competition, providing a clear pathway toward more sustainable transport and mobility.    It will also deliver a more unified technical framework that defines top-level endurance racing Hypercars competing both in the FIA WEC and IMSA in North America, which will be introduced from 2030.  The new framework will provide greater cost-efficiency for manufacturers to compete in endurance racing championships and events globally, boosting potential participation and increasing the spectacle for motor sport fans.   With interest in FIA WEC at levels never seen before, the championship is positioned for continued growth and success over the coming decade. This new deal offers the solid foundation needed to secure its future, marking a milestone moment in the history of FIA WEC.    Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the FIA , said:  “This is not simply an agreement, it is a vital step forward for racing that will secure the future of the FIA World Endurance Championship for years to come.     “This is a deal built for the future, a deal of the century, one that strengthens the collaboration between the FIA and ACO, a relationship that dates back over 120 years, and sets the championship up for a decade of record growth that will deliver real benefits to fans, drivers, teams and manufacturers.     “It has been an honour to play a part in the collaboration that has helped usher in this golden age of endurance racing. I look forward to continuing our work alongside President Pierre Fillon and his team as we build on this momentum and shape an even stronger future.”     Pierre Fillon, President of the Automobile Club de l'Ouest , said: “ We are delighted to see the agreement between the FIA and the ACO extended, reinforcing the strong and long-standing relationship that has been at the heart of the FIA World Endurance Championship since its creation in 2012. This partnership has been built on trust, shared ambition, and a common commitment to the development of endurance racing.      “Together, the FIA and the ACO have created a solid foundation for the continued success and international growth of the championship, and we look forward to writing the next chapter of this remarkable collaboration. Finally, I would like to thank FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem for the great relationship we have built.”      Alberto Villarreal, General Manager at the FIA , said:  “The FIA World Endurance Championship is stronger and more popular than it has ever been before, with a growing and evolving fanbase, and an impressive roster of top-tier global auto-manufacturers.      “The agreement announced today underlines the investment in the championship from both the FIA and the ACO, and our commitment to continue bringing the sport to new audiences. It is a pivotal moment in the history of FIA WEC, and provides the foundation and stability needed for the championship’s ongoing success.”      Frédéric Lequien, CEO of the Le Mans Endurance Management, the promoter for the FIA World Endurance Championship , said:  “This agreement comes at an exciting time for the FIA World Endurance Championship. The championship is experiencing exceptional momentum, with growing engagement from manufacturers, teams, partners, media, and fans around the world. The extension provides a strong framework to build on this growth, further strengthen the global appeal of the WEC and continue to deliver a world-class championship at the forefront of endurance racing. We are looking forward to an ambitious and exciting future for the FIA WEC.”     -   Notes to Editors     The renewed agreement between the FIA and the ACO follows three other significant long-term agreement announcements since July 2025:      FIA and Formula E sign landmark extension to power Formula E World Championship for another 10 years, announced in July 2025 –  information here        Multi-year Concorde Governance Agreement between the FIA, Formula 1 Group and all 11 race teams, announced in December 2025 –  information here        “Deal of the Century” for FIA World and European Rally Championships in July 2026 –  information here         These announcements form part of the FIA’s strategic investment in the future of motor sport, as it continues its mission to grow participation in the sport and provide a safe and accessible platform for all.      The FIA has seen a radical transformation since 2021, and earlier this year  announced  that it had delivered its strongest set of financial results in a decade in 2025, with an operating profit of €6.7m. It also reported an exceptional gain of €20m through the Formula E contract extension.    About the FIA  The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) is the governing body for world motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations globally. It is a non-profit organisation committed to driving innovation and championing safety, sustainability and equality across motor sport and mobility.   Founded in 1904, with offices in Paris, London and Geneva, the FIA brings together 246 Member Organisations across five continents, representing millions of road users, motor sport professionals and volunteers. It develops and enforces regulations for motor sport, including six FIA World Championships, to ensure worldwide competitions are safe and fair for all.    About the ACO   Founded in 1906, the Automobile Club de l’Ouest (ACO) is the creator and organiser of major motorsport events: the first Grand Prix in history in 1906, followed by the 24 Hours of Le Mans starting in 1923. The ACO has also been the organiser and promoter of the FIA World Endurance Championship (FIA WEC) since 2012 and the creator of continental series: the European Le Mans Series (2004) and the Asian Le Mans Series (2013). The ACO organises the 24 Hours of Le Mans Motorcycle Race, the 24 Hours of Le Mans Karting, the 24 Hours of Le Mans Truck Race, and the French Motorcycle Grand Prix on its Le Mans circuits…   The 24 Hours of Le Mans serves as a true technological laboratory focused on automotive innovation. It is in this spirit that the ACO continues to evolve. Sustainable mobility - embodied in particular by MissionH24, which aims to introduce hydrogen to the 24 Hours of Le Mans - is a key objective for the ACO.   Since 2024, the ACO has held the FIA’s 3-star environmental accreditation and is ISO 20121 certified, the benchmark for responsible event management. In September 2024, the 24 Hours of Le Mans circuit was also voted “France’s Favourite Monument.”    About FIA WEC  The FIA World Endurance Championship (FIA WEC), created in 2012 by the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA) and the Automobile Club de l’Ouest (ACO), represents the undisputed pinnacle of the long-distance discipline.   Bringing together the world’s leading manufacturers, biggest brands, top drivers and most successful teams, FIA WEC races around the globe, pushing the limits of speed, performance and durability while encouraging ever-greater feats of strategic skill. If the fast and fearless drivers are the heroes, then the cars are the stars, from their cutting-edge technology to their dynamic design. And then, of course, there is the sound of the engines – that uncompromising, unadulterated roar.   The cornerstone of the calendar is the iconic 24 Hours of Le Mans, an event born in 1923 that continues to serve as the ultimate test for manufacturers seeking to prove their mettle – but every race has its own character, challenges and pitfalls. As a series with a proud history, a compelling present and a thrilling future, FIA WEC remains endurance racing’s global benchmark, continuously setting the standard in the sport and inspiring generations to come. title: New teams join expanded FIA FREC entry
summary: Sport news The Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, and FIA Member Club Automobile Club d’Italia (ACI), the organiser and promoter of the FIA Formula Regional European Championship (FIA FREC), are delighted to announce the teams that have been selected to contest the 2027 FIA FREC season.    Underlining the appeal of FIA FREC, the 10 teams that entered the inaugural season in 2026 reapplied to continue competing in the series. And to further highlight that popularity, two new teams have successfully applied to take part.   It means 12 teams, each entering three cars, will compete in FIA FREC season two for a total 36-car entry, an increase of six Gen2 Tatuus T 326 FIA Formula Regional cars compared to 2026. This rise of participant numbers underlines FIA FREC’s status as the step on the FIA Single-Seater Pyramid between Formula 4 Championships Certified by the FIA and FIA Formula 3.   The existing FIA FREC teams selected for the 2027 season are: ART Grand Prix, CL Motorsport, G4 Racing, MP Motorsport, Prema Racing, R-ace GP, Rodin Motorsport, RPM, Trident Motorsport and Van Amersfoort Racing.   Joining the existing FIA FREC teams for the championship’s second season are Invicta Racing and LN4 Fusion.   Invicta Racing already competes in the FIA Formula 2 Championship, clinching back-to-back Drivers’ titles with Gabriel Bortoleto (2024) and Leonardo Fornaroli (2025). The UK-based outfit currently leads the 2026 FIA Formula 2 Drivers’ Championship with Rafael Câmara ahead of the final two rounds of the season.   Recently established and co-founded by reigning Formula 1 world champion Lando Norris, LN4 Fusion is based in the Veneto region of northern Italy as well as operating a base in the UK. With a strong personnel line-up it has plans to expand into other categories in 2027.   The 10-event 2027 FIA FREC season gets under way at Autodromo do Algarve in Portimão, Portugal, from 8-11 April. Subject to contract, the schedule will include a round in support of the Formula 1 Hungarian Grand Prix. Click  HERE  to find out more.    FIA Single-Seater Commission President Emanuele Pirro said:   “The fact all 10 teams from the inaugural FIA FREC season reapplied to take part in 2027 is a great endorsement of the championship’s importance as a key platform for drivers and teams to develop and showcase their skills and capabilities in a highly competitive environment. We are also very pleased that the appeal of FIA FREC has resulted in two new teams applying to take part for what will be a 36-car line-up, which will only serve to strengthen FIA FREC.”      What is FIA FREC?    Having taken over from the Formula Regional European Championship by Alpine (FRECA) for the 2026 season, FIA FREC is the headlining Formula Regional Championship Certified by FIA and the step between Formula 4 Championships Certified by FIA and FIA Formula 3 on the FIA Single-Seater Pyramid.   All FIA FREC drivers compete in the  second-generation Formula Regional Tatuus T 326  on Pirelli tyres. Not only does the level playing field ensure close competition, it also increases the rate that drivers develop.    Developed by Italian constructor Tatuus in partnership with the FIA, the Tatuus T 326  follows the aerodynamic philosophy deployed in Formula 1 to encourage closer racing, while representing another step in terms of performance and safety. The car features the Race Mode push to pass system, which allows drivers to trigger full engine performance when activated by a button pressed from inside the cockpit. Its introduction is the result of extensive research and development managed by the FIA.   Subject to final FIA confirmation, Emanuele Olivieri is the FIA FREC champion for 2026 after he beat Sebastian Wheldon, Kean Nakamura-Berta and Rashid Al Dhaheri during a four-way title showdown at Hockenheim in Germany last month. Italian Olivieri also won the FIA FREC Rookie title, while R-ace GP from France secured the FIA FREC Teams’ title during the Hockenheim weekend.   Formula 1 drivers Kimi Antonelli, Gabriel Bortoleto, Franco Colapinto and Isack Hadjar are all graduates of Formula Regional while several drivers who raced in FIA FREC in 2026 did so with the support of Formula 1 team academies.    Click  HERE  for more on the FIA Formula Regional European Championship. Click  HERE  for details of the provisional calendar for 2027. title: Formula 1 returns to Africa with 10 year agreement to race in Rwanda
summary: Sport news The agreement marks a defining moment in Formula 1's history and will see the sport return to the African continent for the first time since 1993. Racing in Africa has been a long-standing ambition for Formula 1, and today's announcement follows years of collaboration to ensure the right foundations, with the best partner, are in place to deliver a successful, sustainable and world-class Grand Prix for generations to come.  The long-term agreement will see the first race in the country take place once the new purposebuilt circuit in Bugesera, Rwanda, has been completed, which is expected to be early in the next decade. The new track will be developed to FIA Grade 1 standards as part of a wider sports, tourism, infrastructure, and commercial development project led by the Rwanda Development Board.  Located approximately 40 kilometres south of Kigali and adjacent to the new Kigali International Airport, the circuit will be designed to work in harmony with the natural landscape, using the area's elevation changes to create a unique and challenging racing experience while delivering exceptional viewing opportunities for fans. Beyond race weekends, the venue will serve as a year-round destination capable of hosting international motorsport, major events, conferences and entertainment, helping to drive long-term economic growth and investment across the region.  The announcement reflects Formula 1's continued commitment to expanding its global reach and connecting with new audiences around the world. Africa represents one of the most exciting growth opportunities for the sport, with more than 100 million fans already following Formula 1 across the continent and almost 60% of fans in key Sub-Saharan African markets under the age of 35.  Rwanda has established itself as one of Africa's leading destinations for international events, successfully hosting major sport and global gatherings including the UCI Road World Championships, the ICC Women’s Challenge Trophy, 2023 FIFA Congress, the Basketball Africa League, the 2024 FIA General Assemblies and the FIA Awards Ceremony. The Formula 1 African Grand Prix, presented by Visit Rwanda, represents the next chapter in the country's ambition to become a globally recognised hub for sport, tourism, innovation and business.  More than simply bringing Formula 1 back to Africa, the project is designed to create a legacy by supporting tourism, attracting investment, developing local talent and creating new opportunities for communities and businesses. Together, Formula 1, the Government of Rwanda and the Rwanda Development Board share a vision to build an event that generates meaningful economic and social impact while inspiring future generations across the continent. Further details regarding the inaugural race date, circuit development milestones and race weekend plans will be announced in due course.   Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the FIA, said:   “The return of the FIA Formula One World Championship to Africa is a historic moment for our sport and an important step in the continued global growth of motorsport. Rwanda has demonstrated a strong commitment to delivering a world-class event, and the FIA will work closely with FOM and our partners as this new circuit is developed to the highest international standards.    “This agreement is also about creating a lasting legacy, inspiring new generations, developing talent and opening new opportunities for motorsport across Africa and beyond. Increasing accessibility is at the heart of the FIA’s mission, and we have a responsibility to ensure that our sport continues to grow at every level, reaching new communities and creating opportunities for people in every corner of the world.    “I congratulate President Paul Kagame on this landmark moment for his nation and share my thanks with Stefano Domenicali and all those whose collaboration has made this exciting new chapter possible.”    Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of Formula 1 Group, said:   “Today is a landmark moment for Formula 1. With Rwanda joining the calendar from the next decade, our sport will race in every inhabited continent, bringing the World Championship closer than ever to fans around the globe. Africa has always been part of Formula 1's future, and from the beginning we were determined to return in the right way, with the right partner, a long-term commitment and a clear vision for creating meaningful impact. I would like to thank His Excellency Paul Kagame, President of the Republic of Rwanda, the Government of Rwanda, the Rwanda Development Board, FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem and everyone whose dedication and collaboration have made this possible.    “This is about much more than hosting a Grand Prix. Together, we can create lasting economic and social benefits through tourism, investment, skills development and local business growth, ensuring the positive impact of this event is felt for generations. For our fans, this is an especially exciting moment. Africa is home to more than 100 million Formula 1 fans, and that number continues to grow rapidly. We are bringing the excitement, energy and drama of Formula 1 closer to millions of people who have waited a long time to see our sport return to the continent, and we look forward to writing an exciting new chapter together."    His Excellency Paul Kagame, President of the Republic of Rwanda, said:   “Today belongs to Africa. For more than three decades, the world's premier motorsport championship has raced without this continent, and that changes with this agreement. Rwanda is proud to host the Formula 1 African Grand Prix, and to share this moment with more than 100 million fans across Africa, many of them young people who deserve to see the sport at home and to see themselves in it: as engineers, technicians, entrepreneurs and, one day, drivers. This tenyear partnership is also an investment in Rwanda's future. The circuit in Bugesera, alongside the new international airport, will bring jobs, skills, tourism and new business to our country and our region for decades to come, because our aim was never a single race weekend, but a lasting benefit for our people. I thank Stefano Domenicali, Formula 1 and Mohammed Ben Sulayem for the work that has brought us to this day. We look forward to welcoming the world to Rwanda for the African Grand Prix.”         FIA  Formula 1  F1   Sport 1SportF1FIAFormula 100 Tuesday, October 13, 2026 - 10:21am  Tuesday, October 13, 2026 - 10:21am

title: FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem meets with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev as Baku Celebrates a Decade of Racing
summary: FIA news His Excellency Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), met with His Excellency Ilham Aliyev, President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, in Baku today to discuss shared priorities across motorsport and mobility.  The meeting, which took place during the Baku Grand Prix as the city celebrated a decade of racing on its iconic streets, provided an opportunity to discuss Azerbaijan’s continued development as a major international sporting destination, its established position within global motorsport, and opportunities to strengthen cooperation between the country and the FIA.  Azerbaijan has become an important destination on the international sporting calendar, with Baku providing one of Formula 1’s most distinctive city-centre settings and attracting fans and visitors from around the world.  The Presidents also discussed the wider role of mobility in supporting economic growth and connectivity, as well as the importance of road safety and sustainable transport as Azerbaijan continues to invest in its infrastructure and international connectivity.   FIA President, H.E. Mohammed Ben Sulayem said:   “It was a pleasure to meet with His Excellency President Ilham Aliyev and discuss our shared ambitions for the continued development of motorsport and mobility in Azerbaijan.    “The success of Formula 1 in Baku demonstrates what can be achieved through long-term commitment, strong organisation and a clear vision for the role that major sporting events can play in bringing people together and showcasing a country to the world. My congratulations on a fantastic ten years of racing and I look forward to many more.    “Our discussions also extended beyond motorsport. As the global federation for mobility organisations, the FIA is committed to working with governments and our Member Clubs such as the Azerbaijan Automobile Federation to make mobility safer, more accessible and more sustainable. I look forward to continuing our collaboration with our partners in Azerbaijan across these important areas.”   President Ben Sulayem’s visit comes as the FIA continues to strengthen its engagement across the region through its global network of Member Clubs and partners, including the Azerbaijan Automobile Federation and its President Anar Alakbarov.  The FIA has placed significant emphasis on growing motorsport participation and strengthening the pathway from grassroots competition to the highest levels of the sport, while using its global mobility network to advance road safety, sustainable mobility and accessibility. Azerbaijan’s position at the crossroads of Europe and Asia, alongside continued investment in transport and infrastructure, provides opportunities for further collaboration across both pillars of the FIA’s work.  The meeting formed part of President Ben Sulayem’s programme in Azerbaijan, bringing together government, motorsport and mobility stakeholders to discuss opportunities to further develop the FIA’s activities in the country and wider region.        ENDS    About the FIA   The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) is the governing body for world motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations globally. title: WEC: Alpine on pole at Fuji after rain leads to qualifying cancellation
summary: Sport news Heavy rain swept across Fuji Speedway ahead of the scheduled start of the LMGT3 qualifying session, which began on time but was red-flagged after François Heriau went off in his #21 VISTA AF Corse Ferrari.  The decision was then taken to cancel the remaining qualifying sessions due to the forecast of heavier rain and fog at Fuji Speedway.  That meant that, in accordance with the regulations, the grid was set according to the best times from the three Free Practice sessions held across Friday and Saturday morning.  Victor Martins’ FP2 time of 1m40.594s ensured that the #36 Alpine will start from pole position, marking the first-ever WEC pole for the A424 Hypercar.  It was a double celebration for the French manufacturer as the #35 car will join its sister Hypercar on the front row, putting Alpine in a strong position to defend last year’s victory at the venue.  Second on the grid should initially have been the #007 Aston Martin Valkyrie, but it was demoted to fourth after receiving a penalty for causing a collision in the morning’s FP3 session.  Starting third on the grid will be the #17 Genesis Magma Hypercar, meaning the Korean manufacturer will begin tomorrow’s race from by far its best-ever starting position.  In the LMGT3 category, the #77 Proton Competition Ford Mustang will start from pole position after setting the fastest FP2 time on Friday afternoon. It marks the first pole position for a Ford Mustang since the Lone Star Le Mans race at COTA in September 2025.       WEC  Endurance  6 Hours of Fuji  WEC   Sport 1SportWECWECEndurance6 Hours of Fuji00 Saturday, September 26, 2026 - 9:08am  Saturday, September 26, 2026 - 9:08am

title: FIA Invites Fans to Help Shape the Future of Touring Car Racing
summary: Sport news he FIA has launched a global survey encouraging fans from around the world to help shape the future of touring car racing by sharing their views on what the next generation of touring car regulations should look like.  As the FIA begins work on a new set of technical regulations for its top-level touring car category, the survey aims to gather views from across the global touring car community on the key elements that should define the discipline in the years ahead.  Top-level FIA touring car racing has evolved significantly over the years, taking many different forms in response to changing sporting, technical and commercial priorities – from cups and international series to the FIA World Touring Car Championship, and from Super 2000 and TC1 regulations to today's TCR platform.  The FIA's objective is for the new class to be cost-effective while remaining relevant, featuring cars that are spectacular to watch, demanding to drive and capable of producing close-quarters racing.  As the FIA begins work on its next technical platform, the survey will help identify the characteristics fans would like to see in the touring cars of tomorrow, from their appearance and performance to the type of racing they produce.  Participants will also be able to share their views on what makes touring car racing unique and which race formats deliver the most exciting and engaging competition.  To take part, visit   TCFanSurvey.com  . The survey will remain open until 25 October, with fans from all regions and backgrounds encouraged to participate.   Alan Gow, FIA Touring Car Commission President , said:  "The FIA is seeking the opinions of touring car fans as it begins to consider what the next generation of FIA Touring Cars should look like. Their input will help ensure that future cars remain relevant and popular. Most importantly, they must maintain or even increase the close and exciting battles that are the hallmark of great touring car racing, while keeping a strict eye on cost control."    Marek Nawarecki ,  FIA Senior Circuit Sport Director , said:  "The future of touring car racing should be shaped not only by officials, manufacturers and teams, but also by the people who fill grandstands, watch broadcasts and follow the sport around the world. As the regulator of the sport, the FIA wants to hear directly from those fans. This survey gives them a unique opportunity to help shape the future of this spectacular form of racing." title: Hankook Renews FIA Three-Star Environmental Accreditation
summary: FIA news The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, announces that Hankook Tire & Technology (Hankook), a leading global tyre company, has retained its FIA Three-Star Environmental Accreditation, the top tier of the FIA Environmental Accreditation Programme.   Hankook was first awarded Three-Star status in 2024, during its time as the Exclusive Tyre Supplier and Official Tyre Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship from Season 9 to Season 12. This year's renewal was granted after a thorough third party audit, confirming that the FIA's Global Partner has maintained the standards that earned it the accreditation in the first place.   Central to the Three-Star rating is Hankook's use of life cycle assessment (LCA). By measuring the environmental impact of its Formula E tyres at every stage, from sourcing raw materials to manufacturing and transport, Hankook has built a system to track and manage its carbon footprint across production. It is this kind of evidence-based approach that the Programme's highest level is designed to recognise.   The FIA Environmental Accreditation Programme has helped close to 300 organisations across motor sport and mobility to measure, manage and improve their environmental performance. Assessments take in the full picture, from senior management commitment to energy use and logistics to waste management and carbon accounting, with Three Stars being the highest level achievable.   Willem Groenewald, FIA Secretary General for Automobile Mobility, Sustainability and Tourism, said:   “Congratulations to Hankook on renewing its FIA Three-Star Environmental Accreditation. Earning our highest environmental standard once is an achievement; renewing it shows a commitment that runs deep. As a Global Partner of the FIA, Hankook shares our belief that motor sport can drive innovation from the track to the road, and this renewal is a fitting reflection of the partnership we are building together.”     Young Soo (James) Kim, Vice President, Motorsports Marketing Department, said:   “We are pleased to renew the FIA 3-Star Environmental Accreditation. As a Global Partner of the FIA, Hankook shares a common vision for sustainable motorsport and future mobility, and we will continue working firmly with the FIA to support sustainable motorsport through innovation and responsible environmental management.”      ENDS    For media enquiries please contact Maria Zander, Corporate Communications Manager –  mzander@fia.com     The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) is the governing body for world motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations globally. It is a non-profit organisation committed to driving innovation and championing safety, sustainability and equality across motor sport and mobility.    Founded in 1904, with offices in Paris, London and Geneva, the FIA brings together 246 Member Organisations across five continents, representing millions of road users, motor sport professionals and volunteers. It develops and enforces regulations for motor sport, including six FIA World Championships, to ensure worldwide competitions are safe and fair for all.    About Hankook Tire & Technology Co., Ltd.    With unparalleled pursuit of innovation and technological excellence at its core, Hankook Tire & Technology continues to actively invest in the expansion of its essential capabilities to deliver consumers the utmost satisfaction on the road. Currently operating in over 160 countries, Hankook has eight manufacturing facilities and five R&D centers around the world, with over 20,000 highly dedicated professionals. Hankook Tire produces exceptional quality, high-performance radial tires for passenger cars, 4x4s, SUVs, light trucks, campers, trucks, buses and motorsport vehicles.   Hankook Tire & Technology actively participates in global sustainability initiatives and is committed to making the world a better place to live. In recognition of the commitment, Hankook Tire was first recognized by the Dow Jones Sustainability Indices World (DJSI World) in 2011 and more recently has been on the list for the past six years starting from 2016. In addition, the company received the highest rating from EcoVadis Business Sustainability Rating for three years in a row.     Sustainability  Environment   FIA 1FIASustainabilityEnvironment00 Friday, October 16, 2026 - 3:23pm  Friday, October 16, 2026 - 3:23pm

title: FIA teams up with Track Titan to support driver development with a focus on simracing and Esports
summary: FIA news The Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, and Track Titan, a UK-based AI driver coaching platform, have signed a Collaboration Agreement to help simracers and Esports drivers develop and improve their performance. Under the agreement, Track Titan becomes an official “Driver Coaching Platform, in Collaboration with the FIA“.  Track Titan’s platform uses advanced analysis tools to provide drivers with personalised feedback and technical insights, helping them understand their performance and identify areas for improvement. Track Titan will provide three-month subscription codes to FIA National Sporting Authorities (ASNs), enabling them to distribute access to their national communities.  The agreement reflects the FIA’s continued commitment to supporting the development of new generations of drivers and expanding opportunities for competitors across the rapidly evolving simracing, Esports and motor sport landscape.  The collaboration will also explore further opportunities to make Track Titan’s coaching accessible to the wider FIA community and to strengthen links between simracing, Esports and real-world motor sport.   Eric Stranne, Esports Sporting Manager, FIA, said:   “Esports is an important part of the FIA’s approach to developing new pathways for drivers and engaging with a new generation of competitors. Track Titan brings valuable expertise in data-driven driver coaching, and this collaboration gives us an opportunity to make personalised performance insights more accessible through our ASN network. Providing subscription access to national communities is a practical way to connect innovative digital tools with drivers and support their development.”    Max Teichert, Founder and CEO of Track Titan, said:   “The desire to improve is universal, but access to great feedback is not. Track Titan exists to close that gap. Together with the FIA, we can give more drivers the clarity, direction and confidence that come from understanding their own performance - and help them see how far focused development can take them.”     About the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile   The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) is the governing body for world motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations globally. It is a non-profit organisation committed to driving innovation and championing safety, sustainability and equality across motor sport and mobility.  Founded in 1904, with offices in Paris, London and Geneva, the FIA brings together 246 Member Organisations across five continents, representing millions of road users, motor sport professionals and volunteers. It develops and enforces regulations for motor sport, including six FIA World Championships, to ensure worldwide competitions are safe and fair for all.   About Track Titan   Track Titan is the world’s largest driver improvement platform, with more than 300,000 members in over 200 countries. It helps drivers understand their performance and become faster and more consistent by transforming complex telemetry and driving data into personalised coaching, actionable performance analysis and clear areas for improvement, supported by live tools and professional car setups.  Available across leading racing simulations on PC and console, Track Titan also works with motorsport organisations, professional drivers and industry partners on coaching and driver-development initiatives that connect virtual training with the wider motorsport ecosystem. title: International GT standouts set for 2026 FIA GT World Cup on the streets of Macau
summary: Sport news Featuring competitors from Africa, Asia, Europe, Oceania and South America, a record eight GT3 manufacturers are represented on the provisional entry list with the returning Aston Martin joining Audi, BMW, Ferrari, Lamborghini, McLaren, Mercedes-AMG and Porsche.  The entry list features a number of FIA GT World Cup winners and internationally renowned GT competitors. Two-time FIA GT World Cup winner Maro Engel returns to Macao alongside 2018 winner Augusto Farfus, while another two-time winner, Raffaele Marciello, has also entered the fray.  They are joined by FIA GT World Cup podium finisher, FIA World Endurance Championship and IMSA champion Earl Bamber, Aston Martin’s stalwart Marco Sørensen, Porsche works driver Thomas Preining, BMW ace Kelvin Van der Linde and Ferrari representative Yifei Ye, adding further depth to the field.    Porsche is the best-represented manufacturer on the entry list with four cars, while BMW and Mercedes-AMG field three cars. Aston Martin, Audi and Ferrari each feature two contenders with single entries from Lamborghini- and McLaren-powered teams, underlining the strength and diversity of the competition.  The field also showcases a blend of established international competitors and leading regional specialists. Drivers such as Dorian Boccolacci, Luca Engstler, Joel Eriksson, Adderly Fong, Alessio Picariello and Alessio Rovera bring significant experience from GT and endurance racing programmes around the world, ensuring a highly competitive battle across the entire grid.  The FIA GT World Cup has become one of the highlights of the annual Macau Grand Prix motor sport festival, combining elite GT3 machinery with one of the most demanding street circuits in international racing. The narrow confines, high-speed straights and unforgiving barriers of the Guia Circuit have produced some of the most memorable races in GT competition, rewarding precision, commitment and bravery in equal measure.  With a field packed with factory-backed talent, championship winners and rising stars, the stage is set for another thrilling edition of the FIA GT World Cup, the ninth in total, as the world's best GT drivers prepare to battle for victory on the streets of Macao, while also celebrating the 20th anniversary of the FIA’s GT3 category.    Coverage of the FIA GT World Cup will be streamed live and free of charge via the FIA’s official   YouTube   channel, while the event is one of four FIA-sanctioned competitions taking place during the 73rd Macau Grand Prix week along with the FIA FR World Cup, the FIA FR World Cup and the Kumho FIA TCR World Tour.   FIA GT Commission President Lutz Leif Linden said:   “As GT3 celebrates its 20th anniversary, the FIA GT World Cup remains the category's ultimate showcase with eight manufacturers participating. The Macau Grand Prix occupies a unique place on the global motor sport calendar, combining one of the world's most demanding circuits with a strong presence in a region that is hugely important for premium manufacturers and their iconic GT models. The strength of this year's entry underlines both the success of the GT3 platform and the enduring appeal of competing for FIA World Cup honours on the streets of Macau, an event that year after year attracts a stellar line-up of drivers from the worlds of GT and endurance racing for a truly unique GT3 sprint contest.”    FIA GT World Cup entry list in numbers     18  entries   8  manufacturers represented: Aston Martin, Audi, BMW, Ferrari, Lamborghini, McLaren, Mercedes-AMG and Porsche   13  nations represented by drivers: Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Denmark, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Italy, New Zealand, South Africa, Sweden, Switzerland, United Arab Emirates   10  Platinum-rated drivers,  6  Gold-rated drivers and  2  Silver-rated drivers entered    FIA GT World Cup winners so far 2015:  Maro Engel, Mercedes-AMG GT3  2016:  Laurens Vanthoor, Audi R8 LMS  2017:  Edoardo Mortara, Mercedes-AMG GT3  2018:  Augusto Farfus, BMW M6 GT3  2019:  Raffaele Marciello, Mercedes-AMG GT3  2023:  Raffaele Marciello, Mercedes-AMG GT3  2024:  Maro Engel, Mercedes-AMG GT3  2025:  Antonio Fuoco, Ferrari 296 GT3       GT World Cup    GT World Cup   SEASON 2026  Sport  Circuit 1SportGT World CupCircuitSEASON 2026GT World Cup00 Friday, October 16, 2026 - 10:24am  Friday, October 16, 2026 - 10:24am

title: Capacity entry lists confirmed for all categories on FIA World Cup weekend at 73rd Macau Grand Prix
summary: Sport news The Federation Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, today confirms capacity entry lists for the three FIA World Cups that will headline the 73rd running of one of motor sport’s most iconic events – the Macau Grand Prix.  From 19-22 November some of the world’s top drivers and teams will contest the FIA World Cups for Formula Regional, GT and Formula 4, during a period of remarkable ascendancy for motor sport in the Asia-Pacific region.  The event shines a global spotlight on what is regarded by drivers and fans to be one of the world’s most impressive street circuits, all made possible through the key role performed by volunteers and officials.  A record 68 racers will fly the flags of 34 countries and territories as they showcase their ability behind the wheel. As a measure of the popularity of the Macau Grand Prix, all available entry spaces in the FIA FR World Cup, FIA GT World Cup and FIA F4 World Cup have been filled.          The 2026 Kumho FIA TCR World Tour, which concludes on the streets of Macao during round eight of the season, adds further variety as leading touring car drivers and their teams chase success in the famous Guia Race, part of Macau Grand Prix week since 1972.  On day 16 of   FIA Volunteers and Officials Month  , representatives of FIA Member Club Automobile General Association Macao-China (AAMC) and the Macau Grand Prix Organising Committee gathered in Macao to reveal the names of the drivers and teams taking part in the Pirelli-supplied FIA FR World Cup, FIA GT World Cup and FIA F4 World Cup in addition to the Kumho FIA TCR World Tour season finale.  Entry lists and more details of the FIA FR World Cup, FIA GT World Cup and FIA F4 World Cup can be found in the links below:    FIA FR World Cup      FIA GT World Cup      FIA F4 World Cup     FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem said:   “The Macau Grand Prix is a legendary event in global motor sport and the FIA is proud to once again be involved in four unique competitions that showcase some of the most promising young talent in our sport.    “The increase in grid sizes highlights the progress we are making to empower racing talent worldwide, and my sincere thanks to the AAMC, Macau Special Administrative Region Government, and the Macau Grand Prix Organizing Committee for their commitment to delivering an exceptional celebration of motor sport for fans.”      FIA Single-Seater Commission President Emanuele Pirro said:   “We’re delighted to count on a capacity 26-car entry for the third FIA FR World Cup. But this entry list is not just about quantity, it’s also about quality and it’s certainly an entry list full of drivers with big potential for the future based on their career results so far. This is a great opportunity for these drivers to demonstrate their talent in a highly competitive environment and on such a prestigious occasion. I’m also expecting big things from the Gen2 Formula Regional car with its push-to-pass Race Mode system, that are new for this year and will bring more excitement to the event.    “The switch to a multi-team entry model for the second FIA F4 World Cup has already paid dividends with internationally renowned teams from 10 countries taking part. The entry list, which expands from 20 to 24 cars for this year, contains plenty of exciting talent for years to come, drivers for whom this will be their first taste of the Guia Circuit. When we created the FIA F4 World Cup in partnership with the AAMC and MGPOC, a key aim was for drivers to progress to the FIA FR World Cup, so it’s very significant that four of the top five finishers in the first FIA F4 World Cup last year will be racing in the FIA FR World Cup this year.”    FIA GT Commission President Lutz Leif Linden said:   “As GT3 celebrates its 20th anniversary, the FIA GT World Cup remains the category's ultimate showcase with eight manufacturers participating. The Macau Grand Prix occupies a unique place on the global motor sport calendar, combining one of the world's most demanding circuits with a strong presence in a region that is hugely important for premium manufacturers and their iconic GT models. The strength of this year's entry underlines both the success of the GT3 platform and the enduring appeal of competing for FIA World Cup honours on the streets of Macau, an event that year after year attracts a stellar line-up of drivers from the worlds of GT and endurance racing for a truly unique GT3 sprint contest.”   Coverage of the FIA FR, FIA GT and FIA F4 World Cups will be streamed live and free of charge via the FIA’s official   YouTube   channel.     Notes to editors:  The Macau Grand Prix has developed into a globally-recognised celebration of motor sport passion, which unites drivers from different championships around the world to test their skills on the most demanding of circuits.  The event also serves as a proving ground for the rising stars of the sport and a hugely important occasion in the Asia-Pacific sporting calendar, inspiring the future generations of drivers and fans.  Taking place for the 73rd time this November, the Macau Grand Prix is another highlight of the long-standing alliance between the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, and FIA Member Club Automobile General Association Macao-China (AAMC).  Growing in strength each year, the partnership includes the FIA Extraordinary General Assembly and Annual Conference, held at the Galaxy International Convention Centre in June 2026 for the second year running.  Welcoming more than 450 senior FIA delegates across mobility and motor sport from 149 countries, the event addressed key initiatives in road safety, sustainable mobility, regional sporting growth and transport innovation.  Other initiatives include growing participation in grassroots motor sport through the Karting Academy for students aged six and over, and karting slalom, while also developing motor sport events and competitions being organised and administered by the AAMC. title: Single-seater stars to showcase their skills in FIA FR World Cup
summary: Sport news Counting for the 73rd Macau Grand Prix, the third edition of the FIA FR World Cup is the first for the Gen2 Formula Regional car.  Developed by renowned chassis constructor Tatuus in close partnership with the FIA, the car follows the aerodynamic philosophy deployed in Formula 1 to encourage closer racing, while representing another step in terms of performance and safety.  It also features the Race Mode push to pass system, the result of extensive research and development managed by the FIA.  Thirteen two-car squads have been selected for the 2026 FIA FR World Cup: Pinnacle Motorsport, last year’s winning entrant, the 10 teams that contested the inaugural FIA Formula Regional European Championship (FIA FREC) in 2026, plus TOM’S Racing, the winning team from the 2025 Formula Regional Japanese Championship. One further outfit representing the historic legacy and international heritage of motor sport in Macau – SJM Theodore Racing – has also been chosen. The full provisional entry list follows:    Following its standout victory in the 2025 FIA FR World Cup courtesy of Théophile Naël after a thrilling slipstream battle on the iconic 6.120-kilometre Guia Circuit, Pinnacle Motorsport returns to defend its crown. It has recruited  Enzo Deligny  from France and Japanese driver  Hiyu Yamakoshi . Deligny, who switches back from competing in FIA F3, was third in the FIA FR World Cup last year while Yamakoshi placed 12th.  R-ace GP brings Italian  Emanuele Olivieri , the 2026 FIA FREC champion and last year’s FIA F4 World Cup runner-up, back to Macao.  Rashid Al Dhaheri , who makes his fourth Guia Circuit appearance, was fourth in FIA FREC this season with three wins. The Emirati is a member of the Mercedes AMG Junior Programme.  Sixth in the 2025 FIA FR World Cup, Frenchman  Evan Giltaire  returns to the streets of Macao as the Super Formula Lights champion. He’ll be joined at ART Grand Prix by Japan’s  Taito Kato , a strong fourth in FIA F3 this season and a former F4 French champion.  Trident Motorsport has recruited Indian  Aryaman Bansal , fifth in the 2025 FIA F4 World Cup, and Poland’s  Tymek Kucharczyk , a leading contender in Indy NXT, who finished 13th in the last year’s FIA FR World Cup from 24th on the grid.  TOM’S Racing’s all-Japanese line-up consists of FIA FREC race winner  Yuki Sano  and  Kiyoshi Umegaki , third in the Super Formula Lights standings in 2026.  Mexican  Ernesto Rivera , a Red Bull Junior Team driver, brings experience from FIA F3 to Macao, where he will race for the first time as part of Van Amersfoot Racing’s attack. The Dutch squad can also count on  Jules Roussel , the winner of the inaugural FIA F4 World Cup one year ago.    Like Rivera, American  Alex Powell  is a Macau Grand Prix newcomer. However, he’ll be able to count on Prema Racing’s vast experience as he builds his knowledge. Colombian  Salim Hanna , who claimed an FIA FREC race win for Prema this year, completes the Italian team’s line-up.  FIA FREC runner-up  Sebastian Wheldon , from the USA, started the FIA F4 World Cup Qualification Race on pole position last season and makes his Macau Grand Prix comeback with MP Motorsport alongside Argentine team-mate  Mattia Colnaghi , a Red Bull Junior driver, who finished fourth in the FIA FR World Cup in 2025.  Two of Rodin Motorsport’s three FIA FREC drivers,  Alex Ninovic  (Australia) and  Reza Seewooruthun  (Great Britain), will front its Macau Grand Prix attack, while FIA FREC race winner  Maksimilian Popov  joins Singapore’s  Kabir Anurag  at RPM.  China’s  Zhenrui Chi , who competes under the Italian flag, and Italian  Matteo De Palo  are CL Motorsport’s Macau Grand Prix representatives with Frenchman  Andrea Dupé  and  Kai Daryanani  lining up for G4 Racing.   Kean Nakamura-Berta , a Williams F1 Team Driver Academy member, has Macau Grand Prix experience from the FIA F4 World Cup in 2025 and brings strong Formula Regional pedigree to the event after he won the Middle East title and finished third in FIA FREC in 2026. Joining the Briton at SJM Theodore Racing is American  James Egozi , the winner of this year’s Eurocup-3 title.   FIA Single-Seater Commission President Emanuele Pirro said:   “We’re delighted that the level of interest we’ve seen in Formula Regional Championships Certified by the FIA this year has transferred to the FIA FR World Cup where we can count on a capacity 26-car entry. But this entry list is not just about quantity, it’s also about quality and it’s certainly an entry list full of drivers with big potential for the future based on their career results so far. And with FIA Formula 3 the next step for many of the drivers taking part, this is a great opportunity for them to demonstrate their talent in a highly competitive environment and during such a prestigious occasion as the Macau Grand Prix. I’m also expecting big things from the Gen2 Formula Regional car with its push-to-pass Race Mode system, that are new for this year and will bring more excitement to the event.”   The FIA FR World Cup is a joint initiative by Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, FIA Member Club Automobile General Association Macao-China (AAMC) and the Macau Grand Prix Organizing Committee.  Coverage of the FIA FR World Cup will be streamed live and free of charge via the FIA’s official   YouTube   channel, while the event is one of four FIA-sanctioned competitions taking place during the 73rd Macau Grand Prix week along with the FIA GT World Cup, the FIA F4 World Cup and the Kumho FIA TCR World Tour. title: Next generation assembles for second FIA F4 World Cup
summary: Sport news Following the highly successful inaugural FIA F4 World Cup in 2025, the event returns to the Macau Grand Prix with a multi-team entry format and more entries after the grid size was increased from 20 to 24 cars.  Twelve teams representing 10 countries each running two Pirelli-equipped Tatuus F4-T421 were selected to contest one of the most important junior single-seater events on the international calendar.  These international-level teams have recruited drivers, that in total, fly 21 national flags and represent Formula 4 Championships Certified by FIA from around the world.  Heading the entry list for Campos Racing are  Scott Kin Lindblom  from Sweden and his Hong Kong team-mate  Kimi Yu Tsai Chan . Red Bull Junior Team driver Kin Lindblom placed seventh in the F4 British standings, while Chan holds second place in the current F4 China standings.  Hitech is represented by F4 British championship runner-up  Theo Palmer  from the UAE and Briton  Jarrett Clark , 10th in his national series.     Monaco’s  Oscar Repetto , who has built experience competing in F4 Italy this season, is joined at Hydrangea Kageyama Racing by Japanese driver  Ryusho Nakazato , a competitor in his country’s Formula 4 Championship Certified by FIA.  Red Bull Junior  Rocco Coronel , who starts the F4 Spanish season showdown from 6-8 November third in the standings, joins current points leader and fellow Dutch driver  Kasper Schormans  at MP Motorsport.  Prema Racing can count on the emerging talents of  Alp Hasan Aksoy  from Turkey and Belgian  Dries van Langendonck . With one round remaining on 1 November, Aksoy is second in the F4 Italy order and the top Rookie driver. Van Langendonck, meanwhile, is the F4 British champion for 2026 and a member of the McLaren Driver Development Programme.  R-ace GP’s Franco-British pairing of  Andy Consani  and  Kenzo Craigie  have competed successfully in Italian F4 this season and are part of the Mercedes AMG Junior Programme, while Rodin Motorsport’s line-up of Canadian  Jensen Burnett  and American  Vivek Kanthan  have impressed in Spanish F4 in 2026.     Noah Killion  from Australia has raced in F4 Italy this season and will make his FIA F4 World Cup debut with US Racing, which will also run its F4 Italy champion  Luka Sammalisto  from Finland.  Malaysian outfit Evans GP brings F4 Italy frontrunner  David Cosma-Cristofor  from Romania and Vietnam’s  Hoai Nam Anh Nguyen  to the FIA F4 World Cup.  Macau-based SJM Theodore Racing’s  Noah Monteiro , the son of 2016 Macau Guia Race winner Tiago Monteiro, holds second place in F4 Spain with one round remaining, while the Portuguese racer’s Ukrainian team-mate,  Oleksandr Bondarev , was a winner on his FIA Formula Regional European Championship debut at Imola last month. A member of the Williams F1 Team Driver Academy, Bondarev also raced in F4 Italy this season.   Yu Yan , who is currently third in F4 China in 2026, and Macau’s  Si Lun Vernice Lao , form local squad Asia Racing Team RFN’s attack on the FIA F4 World Cup.  F4 Italy contender  Ludovic Busso  and  Felipe Reijs  complete the second FIA F4 World Cup entry for Argenti Motorsport. Reijs, from The Netherlands, has raced in F4 Spain and the F4 CEZ Championship Certified by FIA this year.   FIA Single-Seater Commission President Emanuele Pirro said:   “The switch to a multi-team entry model for the second FIA F4 World Cup has already paid dividends with internationally renowned teams from 10 countries taking part. The entry list, which expands from 20 to 24 cars for this year, contains plenty of exciting talent for years to come, drivers for whom this will be their first taste of the Guia Circuit as they build their experience before they progress to the next level. When we created the FIA F4 World Cup in partnership with the AAMC and Macau Grand Prix Organizing Committee, a key aim was for drivers to progress to the FIA FR World Cup, so it’s very significant that four of the top five finishers in the first FIA F4 World Cup last year will be racing in the FIA FR World Cup this year.”   The FIA F4 World Cup is a joint initiative by Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, FIA Member Club Automobile General Association Macao-China (AAMC) and the Macau Grand Prix Organizing Committee.  It was established to provide an opportunity for young drivers to gain experience of Guia Circuit before stepping up to the FIA FR World Cup in future seasons in line with the FIA Junior Single-Seater Pyramid.  Coverage of the FIA F4 World Cup will be streamed live and free of charge via the FIA’s official   YouTube   channel, while the event is one of four FIA-sanctioned competitions taking place during the 73rd Macau Grand Prix week along with the FIA FR World Cup, the FIA GT World Cup and the Kumho FIA TCR World Tour. title: INTERNATIONAL COURT OF APPEAL - Hearing October 15, 2026
summary: Sport news The following hearing of the International Court of Appeal will take place in Paris:   Hearing     Case ICA-2026-12-13: Appeals lodged on behalf of Mr Gianmarco Ercoli and Mr Raphael Lessard against the Decision of the National Court of Appeal of the Fédération Française du Sport Automobile (FFSA) dated 24 July 2026, which ruled on an appeal lodged against Decisions No. 09 and No. 10 dated 7 June 2026 of the Stewards of the 2026 NASCAR GP UK, counting towards the 2026 NASCAR Euro Series.    During the 2026 NASCAR GP UK, held from 5 to 7 June 2026 at Brands Hatch (United Kingdom), Mr Gianmarco Ercoli and Mr Raphael Lessard drove Car No. 11 of ALUMITEC Racing in the V8GP and OPEN Drivers Championships respectively.  On 7 June 2026, following the replacement of the engine of Car No. 11, the Technical Delegate reported to the Stewards that the Team had refused to provide the engine for inspection.  The Stewards subsequently issued Decisions No. 09 and No. 10, finding a breach of Article 19 of the 2026 NASCAR Euro Series Technical Regulations. They imposed the exclusion of Mr Ercoli from the Event and of Mr Lessard from Race 1 of the OPEN Drivers Championship.  On 24 July 2026, the FFSA National Court of Appeal rejected the appeals and upheld the Stewards’ Decisions.  On 27 August 2026, the Appellants lodged appeals against that decision before the ICA. The two appeals will be examined jointly.   When   09:00 hrs  Thursday, 15 October 2026   Where   FIA – 8 place de la Concorde – 75008 Paris (Salle du Comité, 5th floor).   Decision   The decision will be published as soon as possible after the hearing.   Accreditation   Requests for accreditation must be sent by email to the FIA Press Office ( sgomez@fia.com ) on the official letterhead paper of the publication or other medium requesting accreditation, no later than Tuesday 13 October 2026 at noon (French time).  The accreditation request must be signed by the Chief Editor or the Head of a Department (specify which) of the relevant publication, or medium.  The accreditation request must include the following:  i) the hearing and the date for which the accreditation is requested;  ii) name of the journalist and photocopy of their professional press card (currently valid);  iii) email address to which the FIA can send an answer.
